Abhishek Khaitan: 
Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, and thank you for joining us 
on Radico Khaitan's Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call.  
The second quarter of FY27 has been the strongest in our history with 
record volume, revenue and profitability. During the quarter, IMFL 
volume stood at over 10 million cases, revenue at Rs. 1,746 crores and 
EBITDA at Rs. 356 crores, with an EBITDA margin of 20.4%. Two 
quarters in, the consistency of this delivery gives us great confidence 
in the year ahead.

Premiumization remains at the heart of this performance. Our Prestige 
& Above portfolio grew 36% in volume during the quarter, well ahead 
of the industry and continues to enrich our mix with every passing 
quarter.  
In vodka, the structural shift we have spoken about is gathering pace, 
with the category’s share of IMFL reaching 6.3% in Q2. Flavours are 
driving this change, and Magic Moments is shaping it. In August, we 
launched Magic Moments Aam Panna, bringing a nostalgic flavour 
cherished in every Indian household into a contemporary format, 
supported by a digital-first campaign. Consumer response has been 
encouraging and tertiary offtake across the Magic Moments family 
remains healthy. 
 
In whisky, After Dark's modern new look is resonating well in the 
largest segment of the market, and we are extending it to more states. 
8PM Premium Black whisky continues to gain momentum and market 
share, while Royal Ranthambore continues to perform well across civil 
and CSD channels. 
Our luxury portfolio, including Rampur Indian Single Malt, Jaisalmer 
Indian Craft Gin and Virasat Indian Single Malt continue to receive an 
exceptional response from connoisseurs in India and abroad and we 
are steadily taking Virasat to new states. Brand advocacy remains 
central to this effort. During the quarter, we continue to focus on 
advocacy sessions in the on-trade, supported by curated consumer 
experiences, key account partnership and premium shops in shop 
formats at retail.  
The policy environment across key states continues to be progressive 
and supportive, and we see this as a meaningful tailwind for organized 
premium-led players like Radico in the years ahead.  
Internationally, we also became the first Indian spirits company to be 
present across 4 major U.K. airports, a proud moment for the Indian 
whisky in the home of Scotch and we continue to progress towards our 
target of 100 travel retail outlets in the times to come.  
At the same time, the global environment has turned increasingly 
volatile. We are seeing continued volatility in the raw material and 
packaging costs. We are managing this through sharper procurement, 
value engineering, our integrated manufacturing platform and a richer 
product mix. These levers give us the resilience to stay on the course.

Looking ahead, we have upgraded our Prestige & Above volume 
growth to 30% in FY27, and we remain confident of sustaining an 
EBITDA margin of around 20% for the year. 
 
Before I close, an important update on our leadership. Effective today, 
Dilip Banthiya joins the Board as Executive Director and CFO, bringing 
his deep financial, capital allocations and alcobev industry experience 
to the Board. Saket Somani has been elevated to Deputy CFO with an 
expanded mandate across strategy, financial planning, Investor 
Relations and digital transformation. These elevations reflect our 
belief in nurturing talent from within.  
As we enter the festive season, I would like to wish you all and your 
families a very happy and prosperous Diwali. 
 
With that, I would now like to hand over the call to our Executive 
Director and CFO, Dilip Banthiya, for a detailed review of our financial 
and operational performance. Thank you. 
Dilip Banthiya: 
Thank you, Abhishek. Thank you, everyone, for joining us on this call 
today. Before I begin, I would like to thank the Board for their 
confidence in me.  
The momentum we built in the first quarter was sustained through Q2 
with strong volume growth, higher profitability and improved returns. 
Our performance reflects the resilience of our business model, driven 
by premiumization, operating leverage and persistent focus on 
disciplined execution, even as the input cost environment has turned 
more volatile. 
 
During Q2 FY27, we delivered a strong all-round performance, with 
total IMFL volumes of over 10 million cases, reflecting a 7% year-on-
year growth. The Prestige & Above category continued its strong 
upward trajectory, recording highest ever volume of 5.28 million cases 
at 36% volume growth. This performance was supported by strong 
brand momentum and premiumization-led mix improvement. Regular 
volume degrowth was due to a higher base of Q2 FY26 after the change 
in the route-to-market in the state of Andhra Pradesh and the impact 
of the policy change in Maharashtra and Karnataka.  
On the profitability front, Gross margin during the quarter is 48.0%, 
representing a 440 basis point expansion on year-on-year basis and 
109 basis point compression on quarter-on-quarter basis. This 

 
 
 
 
 
4 | P a g e

improvement on year-on-year basis is due to the ongoing 
premiumization. Product mix and premiumization added 510 basis 
points and the price increases added 85 basis points. This was offset 
to a certain extent by the recent volatility in the packaging material 
prices which resulted in approximately Rs. 27 crores of financial 
impact. Gross margin was impacted sequentially due to cyclical brand 
mix change and inflation in grain prices.  
Despite an uncertain macro environment, we are confident of our 
margin trajectory in FY27. To mitigate the impact of increasing grain 
prices to a large extent, we had built up higher level of stocks, which 
has supported us through Q2 FY27. 
 
EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 20.4%, expanding by 462 bps 
on a year-on-year basis. This strong improvement reflects the success 
of premiumization strategy, better operating efficiencies, and 
continued cost discipline. It also highlights the benefit of our consistent 
investment in building a strong premium and luxury brand portfolio 
over the years. 
Building on our strong financial performance, both ROE and ROCE 
improved during the quarter, supported by higher operating profit and 
better asset utilization. As the premium and luxury portfolio continue 
to expand, we expect our capital efficiency and return ratio to improve 
further. 
 
During the quarter, we made a deliberate investment in working 
capital to support the strong growth in our premium portfolio, new 
launches and secure key raw material and packaging material amid 
price volatility. This is temporary build, and we expect it to normalize 
during the second half of this year. We remain disciplined in our 
approach to capital allocation, with capex directed towards 
maintenance, 
operational 
efficiencies 
and 
essential 
capacity 
optimization.  
Looking ahead, our priorities remain very clear, driving profitable 
growth, maintaining a strong balance sheet, improving capital 
efficiency and creating a long-term shareholder value. 
With this, we'll now open the line for questions and answers. Thank 
you.
